Spirit of Adoption
SPIR-it uhv uh-DOP-shuhn
doctrinal phrase
From Romans 8:15; the Holy Spirit as He works in the believer the consciousness and assurance of sonship.

See also: Spirit of Adoption

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

The Spirit of adoption is the Holy Spirit considered as He works in the believer the consciousness, liberty, and assurance of sonship—the inward witness by which the adopted child of God knows and enjoys his standing as a son. Paul sets the Spirit of adoption against the spirit of bondage: “For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.” Where the law works fear and the sense of slavery, the gospel, applied by the Spirit, works the free and loving access of a son to a father. The same Spirit beareth witness with our spirit that we are the children of God, giving the believer not only the legal status of adoption but the felt experience of it—the liberty to draw near, the cry of “Abba, Father” rising from the heart, the assurance of the Father’s love. Adoption itself is the act of God’s grace by which He receives the justified sinner into His family and grants him all the privileges of a son, an heir of God and joint-heir with Christ; the Spirit of adoption is the Spirit applying and sealing this blessing to the soul. The dictionary holds the Spirit of adoption as a chief comfort of the believer and a mark of the gospel’s difference from the law. Christianity is not a religion of slavish fear but of filial love; the Spirit who indwells the believer is not a spirit of bondage but the Spirit of the Son, teaching the heart to call God Father, and bearing witness that the trembling sinner has been received into the household and love of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The Holy Spirit as He works the consciousness and assurance of sonship—set against the spirit of bondage—teaching the believer to cry “Abba, Father” and witnessing that he is a child of God.

SPIRIT OF ADOPTION, the Holy Spirit working the assurance of sonship.

Set against “the spirit of bondage again to fear.”

Works the free and loving access of a son to his Father.

Teaches the heart to cry, “Abba, Father.”

📖 Key Scripture

Rom 8:15 — "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father."

Rom 8:16 — "The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:"

Gal 4:6 — "And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father."

Gal 4:7 — "Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The believer’s filial liberty is lost back into a religion of slavish fear, or presumed without the Spirit’s true witness.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the difference between the spirit of bondage and the Spirit of adoption. Christianity is not a religion of slavish fear, in which the soul cowers before God as a slave before a harsh master, but of filial love, in which the adopted child draws near crying “Abba, Father.” Many believers live still under a spirit of bondage, knowing the law’s fear but not the gospel’s liberty; the Spirit of adoption is given to lead them into the freedom and assurance of sons.

The doctrine must be guarded from presumption on the other side—the false assurance that claims the witness of the Spirit without the Spirit’s true work, or that severs sonship from the holiness and obedience that mark God’s real children. The dictionary holds the genuine doctrine: the Spirit of adoption gives both the standing and the felt assurance of sonship, bearing witness with the believer’s spirit, working the cry of “Abba, Father,” and producing the love and obedience of a true child. This witness is a chief comfort of the gospel and a mark of its grace: the trembling sinner, justified and adopted, is received into the family and love of God, no more a servant but a son and an heir.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The phrase names the Spirit as He seals the believer’s sonship, working filial liberty and assurance against slavish fear.

expand to see more

Greek huiothesia — adoption, the placing of one as a son.

Set against the pneuma douleias, the spirit of bondage to fear.

“Abba” — the Aramaic cry of intimate filial address.

The Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are God’s children.

Adoption makes the believer an heir of God and joint-heir with Christ.

Usage

"The Spirit of adoption is preached on the believer’s assurance of sonship."

"It is set against a religion of slavish fear."

"Its witness is held genuine against both bondage and presumption."
